name: Minimum broadcast graphs on 23–25 vertices: improve the remaining edge bounds
compute_profile: laptop-hours to laptop-days for constrained graph search with embedded five-round schedules; certificate checks take seconds
statement: Mohammadhossein Fakharan’s November 2025 Concordia PhD thesis, Dimensional Broadcast Schemes and Their Applications in Broadcast Graphs, section 1.3, printed pages 20–21, lists the remaining gaps through n=32: B(23) in {33,34}, B(24) in {35,36}, and B(25) in {38,39,40}. It credits earlier constructions and degree-based lower bounds, including Bermond and coauthors. In the synchronous telephone model, a simple undirected broadcast graph informs all vertices from every possible source in ceil(log2 n) rounds. Each vertex participates in at most one call per round. A call goes from an endpoint informed at the start of the round to an uninformed neighbor. All three cases allow five rounds.
success_criterion: Give a simple graph and explicit five-round broadcast schedules from every vertex, with either 23 vertices and at most 33 edges, 24 vertices and at most 35 edges, or 25 vertices and at most 39 edges. The first two possibilities settle the corresponding exact values using the published lower bounds; a 39-edge 25-vertex graph improves the record, while 38 edges settles B(25). Every source must have its own valid schedule. Also strictly improve the best comparable published result at claim time, including compatible compositions of published objects. State whether the candidate is a composition and identify its components. Values in unmerged pull requests do not set the bar.
verification_method: Check the graph has exactly n labeled vertices, no loops or parallel edges, and the claimed number of edges. For each of n sources initialize only that source as informed. In each round verify that each listed pair is an edge, pairs form a matching, and one endpoint was informed at the start of the round while the other was not. Update all calls simultaneously. After at most five rounds all n vertices must be informed. The entire certificate contains at most n(n−1) transmissions and is tiny.
status_checked: 2026-10-15 (supplied literature-status date; primary publication re-read 2026-10-24, later literature not independently rechecked)
angles: Start from known 34/36/40-edge constructions and try edge deletion with local rewiring.
Jointly encode graph edges and per-source schedules in SAT, sharing graph variables across sources.
Exploit a graph automorphism only with a verified orbit argument; expand the final certificate to all sources.
pitfalls: Small diameter does not ensure a five-round broadcast under one-call-per-vertex contention.
A schedule from one source is insufficient.
A newly informed vertex can transmit in the next round.
Allowing six rounds changes the problem.
The thesis gives the published numerical gaps; later exact-case literature was not independently rechecked.
